description: Slovenian AML supervisor Urad RS za preprečevanje pranja denarja (Office for Money Laundering Prevention) and the Ministry of Finance were not searched in this pass, although both publish binding guidance affecting banks and PSPs.

Slovenian significant banks are supervised by the ECB/SSM and appear in EBA/ESMA/EIOPA EU-level registers (credit institutions register, payment institutions register under PSD2, ESMA prospectus register). These EU pointers were not enumerated here.

Banka Slovenije's statistical data warehouse / time-series download interface (beyond the HTML statistics landing pages) was not identified; whether an SDMX or bulk-download endpoint exists for payment statistics is unknown.
a-tvp.si appears bot-defended (403), so its registers, enforcement decisions and prospectus pages are currently uncollectable with a plain HTTP client.
Archive depth of BS press releases and ATVP enforcement listings was not established (how far back pagination goes, whether older items are retired).
Deep links for the LJSE financial calendar and for per-issuer SEOnet archive pages were not pinned down; only homepage/sitemap entry points are recorded.

Most Slovenian payment-services firms and POS/IT suppliers to banks are unlisted d.o.o. entities whose only public artefact is the AJPES annual report; there is no press-release or IR stream for them in this cell.
Free JOLP access covers only the last five business years; longer time series for trend analysis are not obtainable through the public interface.
Commercial Slovenian credit/company-data aggregators that resell AJPES filings (bonitete providers) were not searched in this pass.
No URL in this slice was fetched to confirm reachability; all entries rest on search-result evidence and observed URL patterns.
No verified English IR/press-release endpoints for OTP Slovenija (post-NKBM/SKB merger), Addiko Bank Slovenija, Gorenjska Banka, Sparkasse, Delavska hranilnica or the processor Bankart.
This cell is by definition the English layer, but the pass confirmed that English renderings are systematically partial (SEOnet legal caveat; SL-only investor news pages on nlbgroup.com/si-sl).
Regional aggregators were sampled but their Slovenia-specific banking cadence (items per month, lag versus the SL original) was not measured.
Rating agencies were only partly covered: S&P and Fitch actions on Slovenian banks were seen through press restatements, and Moody's was not covered at all in this pass.

EU-level supervisory and statistical publishers that render Slovenian bank data in English (ECB SSM, EBA transparency exercise/risk dashboard, ECB payments statistics) were not enumerated in this cell.

Smaller Slovenian banks and savings banks (SKB/OTP-merged entities, Gorenjska banka/AIK, Addiko Bank Slovenia, Delavska hranilnica, Sparkasse) were not individually checked for rating-agency coverage.

Bank annual-report auditor's opinions (revizorjevo mnenje / revizijsko poročilo) inside Slovenian bank annual reports were not harvested, nor was the mapping of which Big Four firm audits which Slovenian bank.
IT/operational and cyber risk assessments of Slovenian banks (DORA readiness, ICT risk in SREP, ECB cyber stress test results with a Slovenia line) were not searched in this pass.
Domestic academic/think-tank assessors of the banking sector (University of Ljubljana Faculty of Economics, IMAD/UMAR, Bank Association of Slovenia analyses) were not covered as third-party analysts.
Licensed terminal/aggregator routes to agency research (Bloomberg, LSEG, Alacra, CBonds) were only glimpsed via alacrastore.com search hits and not assessed.
Careers endpoints missing for Addiko Bank Slovenija, Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica, Banka Slovenije, Sparkasse/Steiermärkische SI, and SI savings banks (hranilnice).

Payment/fintech vendors and integrators serving SI banks (beyond Halcom and Bankart) are unmapped — e.g. Comtrade, Marand, Endava/Adacta-type integrators, e-money and PSP licensees registered with Banka Slovenije.
No archiving/snapshot strategy exists for ephemeral ads, and no check was made for RSS/JSON feeds or an API on ZRSZ, Optius or Zaposlitev.net.
LinkedIn — the best source for named stacks, seniority and headcount growth — is ToS/login-restricted, leaving no compliant automated route.

Adjacent hiring-signal channels were not explored: student-work agencies (študentski servis) which banks use for pilot teams, procurement/consulting-body-shop tenders, and internship/scholarship programmes (štipendije) that flag multi-year capability plans.

English-language coverage relied largely on LinkedIn; international-group career portals (UniCredit group, Intesa Sanpaolo group, OTP group, Addiko group) that carry SI-located requisitions in EN were not enumerated.

No events run by card schemes and processors active in Slovenia (Mastercard Slovenija, Visa CEE, Bankart, Diners Club Slovenija) or by fintech/payments startups were identified, despite Mastercard Slovenija appearing as a WEBSI award winner.

Security/anti-fraud conferences (e.g. Infosek) and retail/commerce conferences (Slovenian retail and e-commerce trade events) where payment-acceptance topics are discussed were not covered in this pass.
Past-edition conference microsites (financna-konferenca.si, dpc.delo.si, ZBS posvet pages) are typically overwritten each year; no snapshot strategy was established.

Slovenian coverage is strong for events and awards, but English-language coverage of Slovenian speakers at international events (Sibos, EBAday, Money20/20, EBA) relies on third-party lists; no systematic search of speaker directories by nationality was performed.
LinkedIn is where Slovenian bank executives most often post about speaking slots and award wins, but it was not assessed here due to access and terms considerations.

Utilities and telco billers beyond Telekom Slovenije (e.g. A1 Slovenija, Telemach, Elektro distribution companies, water/heating utilities) were not covered; these are among the largest recurring-collection and direct-debit users in the country.
Tolling (DARS e-vinjeta, DarsGo) and airport/duty-free acceptance are entirely uncovered in this pass.

Hospitality, fuel-adjacent and QSR acceptance (hotels, restaurant chains, tourism operators) is not represented, although these are heavy tip/tourist-card acceptance segments in a tourism-dependent economy.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin: only one English query was run and it returned mostly non-Slovenian vendor and market-overview material rather than merchant primary sources.
Merchant-side acquirer and PSP relationships are almost never disclosed publicly; only Big Bang's marketplace seller terms (naming Mangopay) exposed one directly in this pass.
No confirmed public register of DPA fines/decisions naming Slovenian banks or payment providers.

Only Addiko and DBS notice pages were located in this pass; equivalent 'obvestila' pages for NLB, OTP, SKB, Nova KBM legacy brands, Sparkasse, Delavska hranilnica, BKS, Intesa Sanpaolo, Gorenjska banka and non-bank PSPs (Bankart, Moneta/Mobilna denarnica, Flik participants) were not individually enumerated.

Consumer-complaint community channels (Slo-Tech forum, Reddit r/Slovenia, Facebook groups, Google/Trustpilot reviews of bank apps, App Store/Google Play review streams) were not searched in this pass.
ATVP (securities market agency) complaint channel and the Ministry of Economy consumer advisory line / VOP (vsedrzavna) consumer portal were identified only indirectly and not fetched.

sodnapraksa.si was confirmed to contain banking/payment consumer rulings, but no systematic query set or result-volume estimate was built for terms such as 'neodobrena plačilna transakcija', 'zloraba plačilne kartice', 'ZPlaSSIED'.
SEOnet per-issuer deep link and scraping mechanics unresolved for the statutory Slovenian disclosure venue.
London GDR regulatory-news stream (RNS) not pinned to a canonical URL.
Webcast/Q&A content is audio-visual only; no text pipeline defined.
The ~10 sell-side brokers covering NLB are named on the analyst-coverage page but their individual research/publication channels were not scouted.
Pre-2019 disclosures (pre-IPO and IPO-period material) are partly on legacy nlb.si paths and were only sampled, not enumerated.
Cell coverage is sl+en only; NLB Group also publishes a Serbian locale (sr) on the media centre, and subsidiary banks disclose locally in SEE languages.

Only Addiko's listed parent was worked through. The IR/segment surfaces of OTP Bank Nyrt. (Budapest), Intesa Sanpaolo / Privredna banka Zagreb, UniCredit S.p.A., Erste Group / Steiermärkische Sparkasse, and AIK banka / Agri Europe Cyprus were not searched in this pass.

Parent-group disclosure for these subsidiaries is often published first in Hungarian (OTP), Italian (Intesa, UniCredit) or German (Erste/Steiermärkische), and Serbian for AIK. This pass used only sl and en, per run scope.
No RSS/Atom feed, sitemap, or API was confirmed for any press room in this cell; several sites are WordPress (gbkr.si, phv.si) where a /feed/ endpoint is plausible but unverified.

Hranilnica LON d.d. Kranj was named in the ZBS membership list but no dedicated search hit was obtained for its reports/disclosures page in this pass; the cell's 'savings banks' scope is therefore incomplete.

AJPES JOLP documentation states online access covers only the last five years, with older reports obtainable only at AJPES offices; several issuer sites (gbkr.si, phv.si) host older PDFs under dated upload paths with no visible index.

Only OTP banka's dedicated ESG/trajnostno poročanje page was identified; CSRD/sustainability statements for the other entities were not systematically located, and Delavska hranilnica's sustainability disclosure is noted as voluntary and limited in scope.
Slovenian ATM/POS terminal estate operators and independent ATM deployers (e.g. bank-shared ATM networks) were not investigated; the cell focused on card processing and instant payments.

Fintech/PSP-licensed non-bank acquirers and payment institutions registered with Banka Slovenije were not enumerated, nor was the public register of payment institutions and e-money institutions retrieved.
Procurement and tender records were not searched. Bankart and the banks procure processing, HSM, terminal and gateway technology via tenders that reveal vendor selections ahead of any announcement.
Historical depth is weak: Bankart annual reports were only located for FY2019 and FY2020, and its newsroom archive appears truncated.
Bankart and flik.si were assessed mainly through Slovenian content; the extent and freshness of their English-language trees (relevant for pan-European counterpart monitoring) was not established.
Worldline's and Nexi's Slovenian legal entities (if any beyond Nexi Slovenija d.o.o.) and their local filings were not resolved; only group-level newsrooms were captured for Worldline.
The licensed Slovenian PI/EMI population was not enumerated entity-by-entity in this pass; only Paywiser was confirmed by name from the Banka Slovenije register.
BNPL and wallet startups beyond Leanpay and Paywiser are not mapped; no systematic Slovenian-language sweep was done for terms such as 'digitalna denarnica', 'obročno plačevanje', 'plačaj kasneje'.

Domestic payment infrastructure/processing vendors adjacent to this cell (Bankart, Halcom, and the Flik instant-payment scheme) were surfaced only incidentally and have no scouted source entries here.
No Slovenian press-release wire (e.g. STA / STA Servis or a PR distribution service used by local fintechs) was scouted, although STA appeared in results as the national news agency.
The single most valuable financial-disclosure source (AJPES JOLP) is behind a free registration wall, and two key media sources (Bloomberg Adria, Delo) are partially paywalled.

Several seed and adjacent vendors were not yet resolved to concrete, trackable source URLs: Result d.o.o., Endava's Slovenian banking work, ZZI d.o.o. (e-invoicing/EDI), Marand, Špica, Datalab, SRC d.o.o. and Actual I.T./Unistar own reference pages, and Iskratel/S&T-Kontron.

Card/POS acquiring technology suppliers to Slovenian merchants and banks (Printec, Payten Slovenia local entity, Nexi/Nets, Worldline, PayTech resellers, Petrol/Mercator POS estates) were not covered; the sl seed query on POS terminals returned foreign-bank pages instead.

For several high-value vendor sites the exact news/reference index URL is a hypothesis rather than an observed path (Halcom news index, Comtrade case-study index, Payten clients page, Euronet SI pages).

The HRC 'Aktualno' index was read but publication dates were not visible in the extracted content, so the Hibis implementations (Deželna banka, OTP, Nova KBM, Croatian euro transition) currently lack reliable dating.
Vendor reference and news pages are routinely rewritten when a customer is lost or a brand changes (HRC itself announced a new brand identity), so today's snapshot loses history.

Coverage of vendors serving Slovenian banks from neighbouring markets (HR, RS, AT, IT) was not attempted in those languages, although HRC explicitly operates in Croatia and Comtrade is Belgrade-headquartered.
No confirmed programmatic search/API path for enarocanje.si notices; only individual form-id URLs and a general terms PDF were observed.
CPV code set for banking, payment services, payment terminals and financial-sector IT was not enumerated in this pass, yet all portal/TED filtering depends on it.

Some state-linked financial actors in scope were not individually researched: Kapitalska družba (KAD/Modra zavarovalnica), Zavarovalnica Triglav's state-linked ownership, Slovenski regionalno razvojni sklad, Javni štipendijski sklad, and municipal treasuries.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature — award notices, DKOM decisions, Court of Audit reports and SDH/SID reports are predominantly Slovenian, with only partial English versions.
No backfill route confirmed for pre-2018 Slovenian award notices (e-JN open dataset starts April 2018).
ZBS committees/working groups ('odbori', 'delovne skupine', e.g. for payment systems, cards, AML) were not enumerated; the Organiziranost page was located but not read in detail.
Bančni vestnik article-level index (issue TOCs, authors, abstracts) not harvested; the legacy archive host info.zbs-giz.si/bvarhiv was referenced only via search results and not fetched.

No association was identified covering payment institutions, e-money institutions or card processors specifically (e.g. no SI counterpart to a national PSP association); Bankart-type scheme/processor bodies were not found in an association context in this pass.
Regional chambers (GZS regional units) and the crafts chamber OZS (Obrtno-podjetniška zbornica Slovenije) were not searched; OZS represents small merchants who are heavy POS/card-acceptance users.
Association conference and event proceedings (e.g. ZBS/Bančni vestnik annual banking conferences, 'Dan slovenskega bančništva'-type events) were not directly located.
English-language association coverage is thin by nature — only the ZBS EN mirror, AmCham and SBCA were found in English; most substantive material exists only in Slovene.

No source found yet for the Primorska/coastal and Gorenjska regional press (e.g. Primorske novice, Gorenjski glas), which would carry local branch closures, savings-bank (hranilnica) news and regional employer/bank disputes.

No investigative/long-form outlet identified (e.g. Necenzurirano, Pod črto, Mladina, Reporter). These are where bank-governance scandals, NPL disposals and political pressure on state-linked banks typically break, and they are absent from the seed list.

Journalist- and analyst-level channels (bylines, LinkedIn/X accounts of Finance.si and Delo banking reporters, podcast/newsletter formats) were not enumerated; these often carry the earliest, pre-publication signals.

No press-archive or clipping aggregator confirmed for Slovenia (Digitalna knjižnica Slovenije/dLib, Kliping d.o.o., or the skupaj.si clipping pages seen in results), which would enable retrospective baselining rather than forward-only monitoring.
English-language Slovenian outlets (STA English service, Total Slovenia News, Sloveniatimes) were not enumerated in this pass, though the cell is nominally SL-focused.
